contextMessages.content: 我们正在准备 TokenForge 的访问/刷新令牌轮换灰度。先把已经确认的约束对齐一下：这次改动不能破坏现有会话撤销语义，也不能让客户端在网络抖动时无意中重复完成一次轮换。

上次预演里有一类麻烦：客户端先收到网关超时，随后发现原请求其实可能已经被接受。我们需要避免它把这次不确定性当成一次全新的轮换。
这类情况应按幂等重试来处理，而不是放宽令牌单次使用规则。客户端重试时必须带上同一请求关联信息，服务端也要能区分可接受的重试与真正的重复使用。

补充完整记录：TokenForge 将 retry grace 定为 90 秒，只覆盖瞬时网络错误下同一 refresh token 的幂等重试，用来处理请求已被接受但响应在网关超时中丢失的情形；超过 90 秒就按轮换已完成或令牌已失效处理，不再重放。采用 90 秒是因为它覆盖客户端与网关的重试/超时上界，同时把旧令牌可再次使用的风险限制在短窗口内。

contextMessages.content: TokenForge is migrating its Cognito app client from legacy session handling to refresh-token rotation. The same client serves a browser application and a small backend-for-frontend.
I will keep the migration scoped to the existing client and preserve its registered callbacks, scopes, token lifetimes, and authentication choices unless the migration requires a documented change.
The rollout proposal uses a 30-second retry grace period and enables token revocation. Browser tokens are moving to the safer cookie-backed store.
The rollout should account for concurrent browser retries, replacement-token persistence, and the difference between an individual sign-out and a full account lockout.
The client already has OAuth callback and sign-out URLs, custom scopes, explicit authentication flows, and non-default token validity settings.
Treat those existing settings as part of the configuration contract. A migration command must not accidentally discard fields that are unrelated to rotation.
Our deployment code currently serializes the client configuration as one generated document, so an apparently small flag change can affect the whole document.
The change should therefore begin with an authoritative read of the live client and produce a complete, reviewed configuration update.
During a canary, a browser retry sometimes sees the previous session value after a successful refresh, and a later request is rejected.
The client-side retry path must atomically adopt the replacement session value returned by a successful refresh and avoid reusing a value that has already been rotated out.
The backend has a helper inherited from the pre-migration flow. We have not yet settled whether it remains compatible once rotation is enabled.
That compatibility question is the remaining implementation risk. Validate it against the authentication guidance and cover both the browser retry and backend refresh paths.
Please prepare the implementation plan for the TokenForge client migration, including the configuration update, the supported refresh operation, and the tests needed for the canary.
I will return a concrete, reviewable plan that preserves existing OAuth settings, addresses the replacement-session race, and calls out any flow incompatibility explicitly.

For this migration, refresh-token rotation and the legacy refresh-auth flow cannot be combined: rotation disables the REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH flow at runtime, so ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH must be omitted from the client's explicit authentication flows. Because the client update is a full replacement, first read the current client configuration and resend every existing field together with the rotation setting; do not submit only the rotation flag. After rotation is enabled, refresh with GetTokensFromRefreshToken or the OAuth token endpoint using grant_type=refresh_token, and persist the newest refresh token returned by each successful refresh. Do not use InitiateAuth or AdminInitiateAuth with REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH.
